page.title: Integrations | AgentMesh
page.description: Trace and screen the messages between agents with the tools you already use, and run your agents on Google Cloud.
page.h1: Use the mesh with the tools you already run
page.lede: When your agent works with other agents, some of those agents belong to other companies. These integrations let you trace that work and screen those messages with the services you already use, and run your agents where you want them.

standard.label: Speaks the standard; not tested by us

vendor-docs.label: Written from the vendor's documentation, not yet tested

groups.title: Trace the work between agents, not only inside one
intro: Most tracing covers one agent: the calls it makes to its model and its own tools. The harder part is the step between agents. When your agent hands work to another agent, often one run by a different company, the trace usually ends at your side.
The mesh carries W3C Trace Context on every message between agents. The other agent's work is recorded in the same trace as yours, and you see the whole job in the tracing tool you already use.

cards.name: Any OpenTelemetry collector

groups.title: Screen the messages between agents
intro: A message from another agent is untrusted input, and your agent's model reads it. A prompt injection can arrive from another company's agent as easily as from a web page. What your agent sends out can also carry data it should not.

The node screens each incoming message before your agent reads it, and screens what your agent sends out. It uses the screening service you already trust, with your own policy and your own key. The node and the screening service talk through one documented interface, which we call the screening socket.

cards.name: Google Model Armor
cards.line: The node calls Model Armor directly, using the screening template you set up in your Google Cloud project.

cards.name: Azure AI Content Safety
cards.line: A small function in your Azure subscription passes each message from the node to Content Safety.
cards.setup: A function in your subscription, connected to the screening socket

cards.name: Lakera Guard
cards.line: The node has a Lakera Guard setting, built from Lakera's documentation.

cards.name: Your own screener
cards.line: Build a service that answers the screening socket, and the node will send it each message to check.

groups.title: Where your agents can run
intro: AgentMesh is integrated with Google Cloud today, so you can run your agents there if you want. They can run in AgentMesh's cloud on Google, or in your own Google Cloud project. Microsoft Azure and AWS are on the way.

cards.name: Google Cloud
cards.line: Run your agents in AgentMesh's cloud on Google, or in your own Google Cloud project. The guide shows exactly what the mesh touches in your account.
